A similar thing happended to me before, in a different model, when I was standardizing latent factors for identfication, and then estimating a higher-order factor from them. At the time, using a "marker variable approach" for the lower-order factors solved the issue, but I don't think I can do it in a bifactor model...

It's hard to tell all of what's going on here, but you almost certainly don't want to "standardize" all of the latent growth terms.

Since the Is and Ss have their loadings defined, what you've done in the "lv as scaling" section is constrain the variances of all of your latent intercepts to equality over variables and constrain all of the slopes to zero growth/flat over time.

I suggest you try building up from a smaller model until you've got something that works before going to all 10 (!) parallel processes.

Pat

Il giorno martedì 28 luglio 2020 alle 14:00:35 UTC+2 mal...@malonequantitative.com ha scritto:
It's hard to tell all of what's going on here, but you almost certainly don't want to "standardize" all of the latent growth terms.

Since the Is and Ss have their loadings defined, what you've done in the "lv as scaling" section is constrain the variances of all of your latent intercepts to equality over variables and constrain all of the slopes to zero growth/flat over time.

I suggest you try building up from a smaller model until you've got something that works before going to all 10 (!) parallel processes.

Pat

It's hard to tell all of what's going on here, but you almost certainly don't want to "standardize" all of the latent growth terms.
